# Isochronic Passage Chart

> An interactive globe showing expected door-to-door travel time from each of
> its departure cities (the list is `origins` in index.json) to every land area
> on Earth, combining scheduled air routes, rail from OpenStreetMap route
> relations, ferry crossings, and a road-speed model calibrated against 2,998
> real driving journeys, with check-in, border-control and transfer penalties.
> Air times are fitted to 107,366 ADS-B flight legs. Named after Francis
> Galton's "Isochronic Passage Chart for Travellers" (1881), the first
> published travel-time map.

## What the numbers mean

Times are expected door-to-door minutes: the way to the airport or station,
check-in and security, border control where a zone is crossed, and the journey
out of the arrival airport are all in the figure. They are drawn in 37 bands on
a geometric ladder from under 30 minutes to over 72 hours; the band edges are
`bandEdgesMin` in index.json. A departure is treated as planned, so the first
service is not waited for; onward flight connections are charged an expected
wait at the connecting airport. Rail and ferry legs are charged running time
plus boarding or terminal time, without a headway model yet.

## How it is computed

A single-source Dijkstra runs over one multi-modal graph per departure city.
The ground is 4,091,715 H3 resolution-6 land cells (about 36 km2, 6.5 km
across), refined to resolution 7 (5.2 km2, 2.4 km across) wherever the road
network reaches secondary grade or a metropolitan area lies. Ground movement
between adjacent cells is charged at a per-cell speed derived from GRIP4
road-density rasters, halved inside cities. Flights connect airport pairs taken
from Wikipedia's "Airlines and destinations" tables, resolved to IATA codes
through Wikidata property P238, with block time modelled from great-circle
distance. Rail runs stop to stop along OpenStreetMap route relations; ferries
along OpenStreetMap ferry routes. The per-cell result is dissolved into bands
and shipped as PMTiles at four levels of detail, plus per-origin binary arrays
of time, arrival airport, surface mode and rail station on a resolution-4 hover
grid.

## Known limits

- Flight frequency is a fitted gravity model, not published timetables.
- Rail and ferry legs carry no waiting time.
- Coverage is about 98% of land; the remainder has no modelled route and is
  drawn in a neutral grey the legend names.
- The build that is live may lag the code: `solveRes`, `origins` and
  `modeDetail` in index.json describe what is actually served.

## Data sources

- OurAirports (public domain) - airport locations and service status
- Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) - airline route network
- Wikidata (CC0) - IATA code resolution
- OpenStreetMap (ODbL) - coastlines drawn on the map; rail and ferry route relations
- GRIP4 (CC0) - global road density; itself built partly from OpenStreetMap
- Natural Earth (public domain) - land mask, country borders, populated places behind the urban mask
- GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) - departure cities and the place names under the cursor (cities15000)
- HydroLAKES (CC BY 4.0) - lake outlines drawn on the map
- adsb.lol (ODbL) - observed flights behind the fitted cruise speed and climb/descent penalty

At runtime the page calls two external services: OpenStreetMap's Nominatim
for address search and click-to-address (only when a search is submitted or a
point is clicked), and Google Analytics for page-view counting. Everything else
is computed in the browser from files on this site.

## Links

- Chart: https://worldmap.atik.kr/
- Machine-readable index: https://worldmap.atik.kr/index.json

## Disclaimer

For reference only. All figures are estimates computed from open data and a simplified model. They carry no warranty of accuracy, are not travel advice, and must not be relied on for any journey, booking, or decision. The author accepts no liability for any use.
